Kuvalayamālākathā

Kuvalayānandakhaṇḍana
also called Alaṁkārasthiti (see NCC. I. p. 299a) an. ‘Ekaṣaṣṭyalaṁkāraprakāśa’ (see NCC. III. p. 55b). by Bhīmasena Dīkṣita, of Kanauj; son of Śivānanda an. grandson of Muralī- [Page254-a. dhara; composed a. Jodhpur while Ajitasiṁha was reigning (1680-1725 A. D.). a. adverse criticism of Kuvalayānanda; based on the expositions of Devanātha, Govinda, Jayarāma an. others.
Alph. List Beng. Govt. p.. 8. 28.
. Ref. to by a. in his C. on Kāvyaprakāśa. See S. K. D., Skt. Poetics I. p. 184.

Kuvalāyānandabhāṇa
play of the Bhāṇa class. by Rāmacandrakavi, son of Candraśekhara. Adyar D.

Kuvalayānandalakṣaṇāvalī
alaṁk. probably the Ku. Kārikās. B.

Kuvalayāmoda
alaṁk. by Cavali Rama Sastri; illustrations in praise of a.'s patron Raja Simhadri Jagapati Rao (1853-1911 A. D.). See M. Krishnamachariar, His.. of Classical Skt. Lit., p. 806.

Kuvalayāvalī
or ratnapAJcAlikA nāṭaka on the marriage of Lord Kṛṣṇa with Kuvalayāvalī (incarnation of Bhūmīdevī). by Śiṅgabhūpāla. Ref. to Viśveśvara (a. of Camatkāracandrikā) who is in all probability its real a.

Kuvalayāśva
or kuvalayAzvIya nāṭaka in 7 Acts. by Kṛṣṇadatta of Mithilā.

. Mithilā II. iii. 32. According to Mithilā II. iii. 32 the first five Acts were written in Bengal in 1753 A. D. an. the further Acts, completed in Benares in 1783 [Page254-b] A. D. on the prompting of Śubhanātha Miśra, a. ardent student of vyākaraṇa.

Kuvalayāśvacarita
kāvya, illustrating steadfast love, on the story of Kuvalayāśva (Ṛtudhvaja) an. Madālasā. Q. by Bhoja. See V. Raghavan, Bhoja's Śṛṅgāra Prakāśa (1963) p.. 773, 797.

Kuvalayāśvacarita
Pkt. kāvya by Viśvanātha. Q. in Sāhityadarpaṇa

Kuvalayāśvacarita
or prasannakuvalayAzva nāṭaka in 9 Acts based on the story of Madālasā an. Kuvalayāśva. by Lakṣmaṇa Māṇikya, Rāja of Bhulua in the Noakhali district of East Bengal. Hpr.

Kuvalayāśvavilāsa
